articles.title: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government
articles.description: Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel's 120-seat parliament in last week's general election.

articles.title: Arab-led Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel's next government
articles.description:
Arab-led Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel's next government

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 15:25

        
      
    
      
    
                Alliance’s endorsement gives opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the backing of 67 lawmakers in the 120-seat Knesset
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Yousef Jabareen (centre), leader of Israel's Arab-led Joint List political alliance, celebrates as the first exit polls are announced during Israel's election last week (Ahmad Gharabli/AFP)
                  Off
                  The Arab-led Joint List has said it will back Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government, dealing a heavy blow to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's efforts to remain in power.

The Joint List announced on Thursday that it would "recommend that Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government", bringing the total number of lawmakers backing him to 67 in the 120-seat Knesset.

The decision follows Wednesday's endorsement by Ra'am, another Arab-led party, whose eight lawmakers also backed Eisenkot.

The two parties together secured a record 19 seats in last week's general election, giving them a potentially decisive role in determining who forms Israel's next government.

Netanyahu's right-wing bloc won 53 seats in the 27 October election, while the opposition alliance led by Eisenkot secured 48. A majority in parliament requires 61 seats.
  
    



  



The results left both camps short of the numbers needed to govern independently, making the support of Arab-led parties and smaller political factions crucial to the coalition negotiations.

The Joint List said its unanimous decision reflected public demands to prevent Netanyahu and his government from returning to power.

It also said the endorsement was intended to widen the gap between Eisenkot and Netanyahu and strengthen the chances of replacing the incumbent government.

The alliance, which comprises three Arab-led factions, said its decision came despite the opposition's failure to sufficiently challenge Netanyahu's political direction, incitement against Arab citizens and attempts to undermine the legitimacy of their electoral choices.

However, the endorsements do not necessarily mean the Arab parties will join an Eisenkot-led government.


  

  How an election defeat triggered a carnival of racism against Palestinians
    Read More »


The Joint List has said it is prepared to support an opposition government from outside the governing coalition, rather than take ministerial positions.

Its leaders have opposed joining a government while Israel continues its occupation of Palestinian territory.

Eisenkot and his opposition partners have also faced divisions over cooperation with Arab-led parties. 

The opposition bloc has set conditions for potential partners, including recognising Israel as a Jewish state, supporting military conscription and condemning Hamas.

Some opposition figures have rejected relying on Arab lawmakers, while others have argued that their support is essential to ending Netanyahu's rule.

Eisenkot, 66, has repeatedly rejected the idea of a Palestinian state alongside Israel.

While serving as army chief between 2015 and 2019, he publicly advocated for closer ties with Saudi Arabia, saying the two countries should work together to counter Iran's influence in the region.

He also said Israel would be willing to share intelligence with Riyadh to confront Tehran.

articles.title: JD Vance blames Iran war and support for Israel for failure in US mid-term elections
articles.description:
JD Vance blames Iran war and support for Israel for failure in US mid-term elections

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 10:22

        
      
    
      
    
                Vice president takes apparent swipe at Donald Trump's decision to go to war in the Middle East
                      
                  
                  

  


                  US President Donald Trump with Vice President JD Vance at the funeral service for US Senator Lindsey Graham in Washington, DC on 28 July 2026 (Alex Wroblewski/AFP)
                  Off
                  US Vice President JD Vance has blamed the war on Iran for the Republicans' brutal showing in the mid-term elections.

In an apparent swipe at President Donald Trump's Middle East strategy, Vance posted a lengthy social media post on Wednesday that also criticised US support for Israel.

“The reason we lost is the war,” Vance said, in the post on X.

He said that Republican voters had wanted Trump to focus on the cost of living and inflation, put "America first" and "change our relationship to Israel”, Vance wrote.

"If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest," he wrote.
  
    



  



"But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there."

With 54 seats in the US Senate and 237 in the House so far, the Democrats have swept to power and have the ability to seriously impede Trump's administration.

As the results poured in, Trump took to social media to distance himself from Republican candidates, despite campaigning heavily for them. 

"I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter," Trump wrote on X. 


One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was "composition" – whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up. So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we're going to shock the world? "No," he told me. "We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us." Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026. There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true. But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone. Another pollster – one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were: 1) End the war 2) Focus on cost of living/inflation 3) Put America First 4) Change our relationship to Israel. Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.) In the next few months, there's going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I'm open to the idea that we should change enforcement – by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you. The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night. If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there. I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.
— JD Vance (@JDVance) November 4, 2026


In an interview with the Wall Street Journal, Trump said that the Iran war was partially to blame for the Democrats' sweeping victory.

"Iran was a piece of it," he said. 

While Trump told Politico on Tuesday during election coverage that he didn't want to just "sit around there for two years vetoing everything", the 80-year-old billionaire, who is prohibited from running for a third term, may also feel unconstrained by lawmakers.

Under the Constitution, only Congress has the authority to declare war, but the last US president who sought congressional approval for the use of military force was George W Bush in 2001 and 2002.

articles.title: Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses
articles.description:
Israel's UN ambassador rejects Vance's claim that Iran war was behind midterm losses

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Nadav Rapaport
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 15:17

        
      
    
      
    
                'It’s very easy to always blame Israel for everything, but that is not the case,' says Danny Danon
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Danny Danon at the UN on 20 June 2025 (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images via AFP)
                  Off
                  Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations has rejected US Vice President JD Vance’s analysis that the war on Iran was the “real reason” the Republicans suffered sweeping losses in the midterm elections, and that the party should “change our relationship to Israel”.

“It’s very easy to always blame Israel for everything, but that is not the case,” Danny Danon told Israeli outlet i24 News.  

“I think it’s unfortunate that many made the link between rising prices, mainly oil prices, and the situation here in Israel,” the Israeli ambassador said. 

“The decision to attack Iran was the decision of the United States. It wasn’t our decision. We supported the US effort, and we think it was the right decision.”

The US and Israel attacked Iran at the end of February. The New York Times reported that in the weeks before the war began, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu shared intelligence with US President Donald Trump suggesting that the Iranian people would rise and topple their government in the event of an attack. 
  
    



  



No such regime change has occurred, and Iran has taken control of the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, sending energy prices soaring.

The attendant rise in the cost of living in the US has been a key issue for American voters and one that Democrats have sought to exploit.

Vance takes to X

On Wednesday, after elections saw the Republicans lose both the Senate and the House of Representatives, Vance wrote in a lengthy post on X: “But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone… The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”  

“I think a part of it was Iran,” Trump has said in an interview, despite also saying that he “would have done it again”.

Vance also said in his post that polling had shown him that Trump voters wanted the US to “change our relationship to Israel”, as well as end the war on Iran, focus on the cost of living and “put America first”. 


  

  'I think a part of it was Iran': Trump acknowledges war's impact on midterm election losses
    Read More »


“If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next six years was worth it, then do so,” the vice president said, stating that “everyone knows why we lost”.

Danon said in his interview that Israel would “have to pay attention” to voices in both the Democratic and Republican parties that are critical of his country. “It will be harder for us,” the Israeli ambassador said, in relation to the increasing prominence of anti-Israel politicians in the US.

“We will always do whatever is necessary to protect ourselves,” said Danon, when questioned on a possible deal between the US and Iran following the election results.

In Israel, the losses have resulted in a wave of criticism of Netanyahu from politicians and commentators who believe the prime minister has become “toxic” for both Republicans and Democrats. 

Critics said that following the sweeping victory of the Democrats, Netanyahu can no longer lead Israel due to his unpopularity in the US.

One Israeli former diplomat maintained that the results in the US were the end of “an era of half a century in US-Israel relations”, adding that “what lies ahead is clouded in uncertainty”.

Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi-fired missile in the Medina region

    
    

        
    
                The Saudi-led military coalition said on Thursday it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis towards the Medina region.

“Interception and destruction of a ballistic missile fired by the Houthi terrorist militia in the Medina region,” the coalition spokesman Colonel Turki Al-Malki said.

Earlier, Saudi Arabia's civil defence issued an alert for the Yanbu Governorate near the Red Sea in Medina province.

articles.title: Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina
articles.description:
Saudi coalition says it intercepted missile fired at Medina

    
    

        
    
                The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis on Thursday said it intercepted a ballistic missile fired by the group at the Medina region, home to one of Islam's holiest cities.

The announcement came just minutes after the kingdom's civil defence agency warned of potential danger in the area near the strategic port of Yanbu.

It was unclear if the two events were connected. 

"Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward the Medina region," coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said in a post on X.

The Houthis rejected any suggestion they were targeting the city, saying such accusations were a "blatant and grave falsehood".

"Our operations target only its oil facilities and military bases," the group said in a statement.

articles.title: ‘It will crush us’: Israeli leaders in panic mode over fallout from US elections
articles.description:
‘It will crush us’: Israeli leaders in panic mode over fallout from US elections

    
    

        
    
                Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid warned after the US election results that Netanyahu’s continued leadership would endanger Israel’s security and deepen its international isolation.

"Israel cannot afford for him (Netanyahu), to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid wrote on X.

"The American election results in the morning have one unexpected outcome: they eliminate any possibility of a unity government led by Netanyahu," he added.

להתבטאויות של זיני בלילה ולתוצאות הבחירות באמריקה בבוקר יש תוצאה לא צפויה אחת: זה מחסל כל אפשרות לממשלת אחדות בראשות נתניהו. ישראל לא יכולה להרשות לעצמה שהוא יישאר ראש הממשלה. זה מסכן את הבטחון, זה מסכן את הדמוקרטיה, זה ירסק אותנו בעולם.— יאיר לפיד - Yair Lapid (@yairlapid) November 4, 2026 

Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats party, also sounded the alarm, warning that Netanyahu’s continued rule could push an already internationally isolated Israel towards “international sanctions, international isolation and a collision with the United States”.

תוצאות בחירות האמצע הלילה בארה״ב חושפות עד כמה נתניהו רעיל גם אצל הדמוקרטים וגם אצל הרפובליקנים. אני מתריע: המשך כהונתם של נתניהו ובן גביר עלול להוביל את ישראל למסלול של סנקציות בינלאומיות, בידוד בינלאומי ולהתנגשות עם ארה״ב, ידידתנו ובעלת בריתנו החשובה ביותר.ישראל זקוקה…— Yair Golan - יאיר גולן (@YairGolan1) November 4, 2026 

Jerusalem Post analyst Amichai Stein warned that the results could bring “harsher criticism of Israel, and less willingness to defend the traditional relationship between the two countries.”

His analysis warned that the success of candidates critical of Israel could influence the Democratic Party’s direction ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

articles.title: ‘Israel cannot afford to ignore’: Israeli press reels from Democratic sweep
articles.description:
‘Israel cannot afford to ignore’: Israeli press reels from Democratic sweep

    
    

        
    
                The Israeli press is taking stock of last night’s Democratic sweep of Congress, sounding the alarm over the consequences for Israel.

A Haaretz analysis this morning said Abdul El-Sayed’s victory over pro-Israel candidate Mike Rogers demonstrated “that even strident opposition to Israel is no barrier to winning competitive federal races.”

“El-Sayed won despite AIPAC spending more than $30 million to defeat him in the Democratic primary and another reported $9 million on behalf of Rogers in the general election,” it added.

The Jerusalem Post warned: “The implications of the US midterm elections for Israel could extend far beyond the loss of Republican control of Congress. The defeat comes amid broader shifts within the Democratic Party regarding Israel, the war with Iran, and the strategic relationship between Jerusalem and Washington.”

“One of the clearest takeaways from the election campaign is the political price the war with Iran has exacted on the Republican Party”, the analysis said, referring to the war Israel pushed the US into on 28 February.

“The expansion of the camp critical of Israel, and its growing access to positions of influence, represents a shift that Israel cannot afford to ignore,” it added.

articles.title: US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu
articles.description:
US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu

    
    

        
    
                As news emerged on Wednesday that the Democratic Party had won a landslide victory, regaining control of the US Congress, Israeli politicians, journalists and experts warned of the results' grave implications for Israel's national security, pointing to the declining standing of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the US.

Former Israeli prime minister Yair Lapid, who was re-elected to parliament last week as part of the centre-right Together alliance, said the US election results had "eliminated" any possibility of forming a unity government with Netanyahu.

"Israel cannot afford for him to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid said on X on Wednesday morning.

Recent Israeli reports indicated that US President Donald Trump is applying pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli opposition leaders to form a unity government that will exclude extremists in order to advance his Middle Eastern policies.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats alliance, also described Netanyahu as a threat to Israel's security in the wake of the US election results, which saw progressive Democrats, including Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed – the first Muslim elected to the US Senate – win races across the country.

Read more: US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu



Israeli Prime Minister and Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu gestures as he reacts to exit polls, at his party headquarters during Israel's national election, in Jerusalem, 28 October 2026 (Reuters)

articles.title: US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu
articles.description:
US election results fuel Israeli opposition's push to remove Netanyahu

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
Nadav Rapaport
 on 
Wed, 11/04/2026 - 13:32

        
      
    
      
    
                Israeli opposition leaders warn that the Democrats' sweep of US Congress could threaten Israel’s national security
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Israeli Prime Minister and Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu gestures as he reacts to exit polls, at his party headquarters during Israel's national election, in Jerusalem, 28 October 2026 (Reuters)
                  Off
                  As news emerged on Wednesday that the Democratic Party had won a landslide victory, regaining control of the US Congress, Israeli politicians, journalists and experts warned of the results' grave implications for Israel's national security, pointing to the declining standing of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the US.

Former Israeli prime minister Yair Lapid, who was re-elected to parliament last week as part of the centre-right Together alliance, said the US election results had "eliminated" any possibility of forming a unity government with Netanyahu.

"Israel cannot afford for him to remain prime minister. It endangers security, it endangers democracy, it will crush us in the world," Lapid said on X on Wednesday morning.

Recent Israeli reports indicated that US President Donald Trump is applying pressure on Netanyahu and the Israeli opposition leaders to form a unity government that will exclude extremists in order to advance his Middle Eastern policies.

Yair Golan, leader of the left-wing Democrats alliance, also described Netanyahu as a threat to Israel's security in the wake of the US election results, which saw progressive Democrats, including Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed – the first Muslim elected to the US Senate – win races across the country.
  
    



  



Golan said Netanyahu has become "toxic" in the US, both within the Democratic party and the Republican party, adding that if the Israeli prime minister continues to rule it could "lead Israel onto a path of international sanctions, international isolation, and a collision with the United States".


'Netanyahu’s continued tenure is an immediate danger to our special relationship with the United States'

- Amir Tibon, Haaretz


According to Golan, the most left-leaning leader of the Zionist Israeli opposition, Israel is now facing a choice between a "boycotted, backward, and isolated" country led by Netanyahu, or "a strong, advanced, free, and secure Israel".

"Netanyahu lost the elections. He is dangerous to Israel," Golan said on X, adding "we have no time to waste. We must form a change government now."

The Democrats MP Gilad Kariv echoed the position of his party leader on Wednesday, ruling out a unity government with Netanyahu's Likud party.

Kariv said on X that "anyone who is still talking this morning about unity with Netanyahu does not understand the results of the elections in Israel and does not understand the results of the elections in the United States."

'US-Israel relations comes to an end'

Progressive US Democrats like Sayed, who have been calling for an end to military aid to Israel over its genocide in Gaza, are viewed by Israeli US affairs experts and journalists as a threat to Israel's very existence.

On Wednesday, former Israeli foreign minister Tzipi Livni, a fierce critic of Netanyahu, said that the prime minister can no longer "preserve the legitimacy of the existence of the state of the Jewish people, or our right to defend ourselves, in the face of the views of some of the newly elected officials".


'An era of half a century in US-Israel relations, as we have known it, comes to an end'

- Michael Oren, former Israeli diplomat


Gili Cohen, the diplomatic correspondent of Israel's Kan 11, said the US electoral results are "not only a defeat for President Donald Trump, but also for Israel’s standing" in the US, as the much-needed American military aid is now on the balance.

Amir Tibon, a journalist at the Israeli left-wing newspaper Haaretz, described the election results as "a political earthquake" with grave consequences for Israel.

"Netanyahu’s continued tenure is an immediate danger to our special relationship with the United States," he wrote on X, adding that the prime minister had become "toxic" not only within the Democratic Party but also among Republicans, some of whose leaders are now blaming him for their defeat.

On Wednesday, Trump acknowledged that the US-Israel war on Iran, launched in February under pressure from Netanyahu, played a role in his party's defeat.

"If Israel wants to start rebuilding its very poor standing in the US, it must part ways with Netanyahu," Tibon said, adding that a failure to do so could lead "to very dangerous places".


  

  Aipac and the Michigan Senate race: How the Israel lobby became toxic
    Read More »


The Democrats' landslide victory also raised concerns among right-wing Israeli politicians and commentators.

Journalist Ariel Kahana told Radio 103FM that "Israel suffered a very serious blow" on Tuesday's elections, as Israel "was on the ballot".

"Netanyahu is a burden on Israel," Kahana said.

Political analyst Kobby Barda of the Jewish People Policy Institute think tank said that Iran was the "big winner" of the US elections, while Netanyahu was the "huge loser".

"The face of Israel’s government can’t be Netanyahu anymore," right-winger Barda said, citing his unpopularity rates in the US.

Michael Oren, a former Israeli diplomat, warned that the triumphs of people like Sayed, who he called "a venomously anti-Israel candidate" and "antisemitic", could lead to catastrophic ramifications for Israel.

Oren warned that "the halt of military aid may be only the beginning", saying that intelligence and military systems sharing with the US, entry visas for Israelis and supplies of essential military components were all now at risk. He added that US sanctions against Israel were also a possibility.

"Thus, an era of half a century in US-Israel relations, as we have known it, comes to an end," Oren said, adding that "what lies ahead is clouded in uncertainty".

articles.title: Netanyahu says 'serious suspicions' of foreign interference in vote
articles.description:
Netanyahu says 'serious suspicions' of foreign interference in vote

    
    

        
    
                Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday that there are "serious suspicions" of foriegn interference in the Israeli elections after his Likud party suffered resounding defeats in the recent vote. 

"There are serious suspicions that foreign states have spent considerable sums to influence the outcome of the elections in Israel," Netanyahu said in a video posted on social media.

He blamed "extremist Islam" for "tearing apart countries in Europe", adding that this "challenge" cannot be confronted by "a government dependent on extremist Islam and these Islamist parties, which deny the very existence of a Jewish state".

This comes as Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins consultations with party leaders to form the next government.


אזרחי ישראל היקרים, האסלאם הקיצוני הוא האתגר שמפרק היום מדינות באירופה. זהו האתגר שמאיים גם עלינו. הוא מאיים מבחוץ על ידי איראן וגרורותיה, ומבית על ידי מפלגות אסלאמיסטיות של תומכי טרור. הם חותרים למחוק את הזהות היהודית של מדינת ישראל. הם אומרים זאת בגלוי. הם חותרים למנוע מאיתנו את היכולת להגן על עצמנו מפני אויבינו. ואני שואל שאלה פשוטה: מי יוכל להתמודד עם האתגר הזה? מי שבוודאות לא תוכל להתמודד עם האיום של האסלאם הקיצוני היא ממשלה שתלויה באסלאם הקיצוני ובמפלגות האסלאמיסטיות הללו, ששוללות את עצם קיומה של מדינה יהודית. צריך רק להקשיב למה שנציגיהן אומרים. הם אומרים את זה בגלוי. הם אומרים: “זה כבוד להיות שהיד, זה הכבוד הנשגב ביותר”. “חמאס הוא ארגון צדקה”. והם מקדישים את ההישגים שלהם בקלפי למחבלי הנוח’בה הנתעבים שיושבים אצלנו בכלא. לא רק שממשלה כזאת לא תילחם באויבינו, היא פשוט תפרק אותנו מבפנים. זה בנפשנו. אבל יש ממשלה שכן יכולה להתמודד עם האתגר הזה. ממשלה לאומית רחבה בראשות הליכוד, בהנהגתי, שתכלול את כל מרכיבי הגוש הלאומי ואת כל המפלגות הציוניות שירצו להצטרף. אמרתי את זה במהלך מערכת הבחירות וחזרתי על זה רק לפני יומיים. מה שכל כך ברור לכם, לרוב המוחלט של אזרחי ישראל, נדחק הצידה כלאחר יד על ידי ראשי גוש השמאל. הם עוסקים בהקמת ממשלת מיעוט צרה, ממשלה שנשענת על תומכי הטרור הללו, והם מכריזים מעל כל במה על תנאים בלתי אפשריים שנועדו לסכל מראש כל אפשרות להקים ממשלה לאומית רחבה. הם מעדיפים את האינטרס הפוליטי שלהם על האינטרס הלאומי. ואתם יודעים, ואתם מסכימים גם עם דבר נוסף. מוכרחים להגיע לאמת. ישנם חשדות חמורים למעורבות של מדינות זרות בכסף עצום להטיית תוצאות הבחירות במדינת ישראל. יושב ראש ועדת הבחירות, השופט סולברג, הנחה את השב”כ לפתוח בחקירה ביטחונית. הוא קבע שיש להסיר את כל החסמים בפני החקירה הזו. הוא צודק. חייבים להגיע לאמת במלואה, ללא טיוח וללא דיחוי. טוהר הבחירות הוא יסוד הדמוקרטיה. חייבים לשמור עליו וחייבים לשמור על המדינה שלנו.
— Benjamin Netanyahu - בנימין נתניהו (@netanyahu) November 4, 2026

                Israeli president Isaac Herzog warned prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu other senior officials of a "highly explosive and dangerous reality" in the West Bank amid increasing settler violence.

"The IDF commanders, the police officers and the Shin Bet personnel present a worrying picture of limited tools and a shortage of manpower," Herzog wrote in the letter sent to Netanyahu, defence minister Israel Katz, the Israeli army chief of staff Eyal Zamir and attorney general Gali Baharav-Miara.

Herzog said that the elections in Israel, the US and the Palestinian Authority - which the latter has since been postponed - alongside the olive harvest season are set to "create a highly explosive and dangerous reality".

"A severe flare-up on the ground is liable to carry severe and far-reaching consequences, both for Israel’s security and its functioning as a sovereign state, and for Israel’s international standing, Diaspora Jewry, the Israeli economy, and more," the Israeli president further warned.

He added that there is a "moral disgrace and the stain on us" when innocent Palestinians are harmed, and stressed that "there is no room for this lawlessness in a sovereign state".

articles.title: Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism
articles.description:
Supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and Aipac drive antisemitism 

    
    

          
      
      
        Submitted by 
MEE staff
 on 
Thu, 11/05/2026 - 21:20

        
      
    
      
    
                Vast majority of Jewish voters in US want sanctions against 'violent West Bank settlers' 
                      
                  
                  

  


                  Voting booths at a polling location in Manchester, New Hampshire, are ready for voters, on 8 September 2026 (CJ Gunther/Getty Images/AFP)
                  Off
                  A supermajority of Jewish Americans think Israel and the American Israel Public Affairs Committee’s (Aipac) actions are increasing antisemitism in the US, according to a new poll.

The poll commissioned by J Street, a US-based pro-Israel think tank, shows a deep gap between how Jewish American voters view organisations like Aipac and Israel’s occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, compared to how the state of Israel and its allies in the US portray antisemitism.

The poll says 66 percent of Jewish voters in the US believe that Aipac’s campaign spending against candidates who criticise Israel actually increases antisemitism in the country.

In addition, 60 percent believe that Jewish organisations that label harsh criticism of Israel as antisemitic are exploiting concerns about antisemitism to defend unpopular Israeli government policies.

Notably, 80 percent of Jewish voters believe that Israel’s actions in the occupied West Bank and Gaza are increasing antisemitism in the US.
  
    



  



“Conventional wisdom about the impact of Jewish concerns over antisemitism and what it means to support Israel often misses the mark on how Jews process these issues in America’s political context,” Jim Gerstein, founding partner at GBAO Strategies, which conducted the poll between 28 October and 3 November, said.

“The reality is that Jews express nuanced thinking on these issues that is frequently missing in the extensive media coverage of the Jewish community,” he added.

The US midterm elections marked a sweeping Democratic victory where the US war on Iran and US support for Israel played a central role in races such as Michigan.

Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed won the race there in a historic landslide against Aipac supported Republican candidate Mike Rogers. 


  

  Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
    Read More »


Sayed, who campaigned on cutting US aid to Israel along with other Middle Eastern countries and condemned Israel’s genocide on Gaza, won 60 percent of early Jewish voters, according to a poll by Mercury Public Affairs.

The poll also showed that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who has been smeared as being an antisemite, had a higher favorability rating among Jewish Americans, 49 percent, compared to outgoing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, at 20 percent.

Overall, the poll from GBAO Strategies found that 72 percent of Jewish voters supported Democratic candidates and that 76 percent supported sanctions against “violent West Bank settlers”.

The president of J Street said the poll underscored the falsehood of stereotypes about Jewish voters in the US.

“Jewish Americans have been treated as a political football throughout this election cycle, with politicians and commentators insisting that our community demands unconditional support for the Israeli government. These results tell a very different story,” Jeremy Ben-Ami said.

“Jewish voters overwhelmingly backed Democrats, strongly oppose President Trump and support holding the Israeli government accountable for its actions. They want American leadership that advances peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians, and they are rejecting the idea that supporting Israel means writing its government a blank check,” he added.

articles.title: Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister
articles.description:
Israeli president Herzog deliberates after Eisenkot receives majority Knesset backing to become prime minister

    
    

        
    
                Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot has received the backing of a majority of Knesset members to be prime minister, possibly granting him the mandate to attempt to form the next government.

Eisenkot received 67 recommendations compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The Yashar party urged Israeli president Isaac Herzog on Thursday to hand Eisenkot the mandate to form the next government "as soon as possible", adding that its the largest number of recommendations given to a candidate for forming a government since 2015.

"Benjamin Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister leading a minority of just 46 seats," the party said. "He has no mandate, no majority and no public trust."

While Herzog expressed that the result was "clear", he indicated that he would hold further talks with party leaders to clarify the situation before assigning the mandate to form a government on Sunday.

articles.description:
Iran’s Basij chief praises 'resistance cinema', saying that 'change has begun' in US, Israel

    
    

        
    
                Iran’s Basij commander Hossein Taeb has said that the US and Israel are seeing change amid their ongoing attempts at transforming the Middle East's landscape.

"Today, we say that change has begun in America and Israel, and we will soon see it across different areas," he said during the closing ceremony of the 19th International Resistance Film Festival in Tehran.

His highlighted the use of media and film as a way of "disrupting America’s media monopoly", describing it as "resistance cinema".

"The staging of this festival under such circumstances signifies that - much like a combatant who never abandons their launchers during military defence - an artist engaged in the 'perceptual battlefield' does not desert their post, even under the shadow of war, economic siege, or any other threat," he said.

"Through their portrayal of the Resistance, they inflict a new defeat upon the enemy."

Referencing US-Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, Iraq and Syria, Taeb said: "All these crimes took place; children were killed, and the oppressed peoples of the region suffered. Yet, the true losers in this conflict were the United States and Israel."
